chunks: From him, from his father, from Safwan, from Abu Makhlad al-Sarraj, from Isa ibn Hassan, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Every lie, its owner would be questioned about it one day, except for a lie in three (matters): A man plans regarding his battle (in times of war) so it would be dropped from him; or a man who reconciles between two, saying to this one with other than what this had one had been said with, intending the reconciliation with that what is between the two; or a man who promises his family something and he does not intend to complete for them.
ai.seo_question: What are the three exceptions to the rule that every lie is sinful in Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates the principle of 'takhrij al-kadhib' (extraction of falsehood) by identifying three specific contexts where lying is not only permissible but excused: military strategy (as seen in the Prophet's use of deception in battle), reconciliation between disputing parties (sulh), and promising one's spouse or family without intent to fulfill (wa'd). This classification highlights the Shia scholarly view that the moral weight of a lie depends on its purpose, elevating social harmony and strategic necessity above literal truthfulness in these limited domains.

en.hubeali: From him, from his father, from Safwan, from Abu Makhlad, from Isa Bin Hassan who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Every lie, its owner would be Questioned about it one day except for the lie regarding three (matters) – A man plans regarding his battle (in times of war) so it would be dropped from him; or a man who reconciles between two, saying to this one with other than what this had one had been said with, intending the reconciliation with that what is between the two; or a man who promises his family something and he does not intend to complete for them’.
en.sarwar: 18. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from his father from Safwan from abu Mukhallad al-Sarraj from ‘Isa ibn Hassan who has said the following: “

I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘A person lying will be held accountable for all kinds of lies except three kinds: a man plotting in his fight will not be held accountable, a man trying to establish peace between antagonistic parties who may say something other than a party may have said with the intention to establish peace between them or a man who may promise his family something but he does not want to complete it.’”
